item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe treats the heme-binding four-helical bundle as a shared membrane-protein fold, not as a single homologous superfamily. In the SCOPe hierarchy these proteins are in class f, Membrane and cell-surface proteins and peptides, under fold f.21, Heme-binding four-helical bundle, but they are split at the superfamily/family level: f.21.1 Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, f.21.2 Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits, and f.21.3 Respiratory nitrate reductase gamma chain. That fold-level co-classification supports using the same broad four-helix heme-binding architecture as a structural analogy; it does not justify merging the transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, fumarate-reductase membrane anchors, and nitrate-reductase gamma chains into one homologous superfamily, transferring detailed function or residue-level heme/quinone-site annotations across them, or choosing representatives/templates as though all f.21 domains were close homologs.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
